newsitem.title: INDIA: India hopes for more insurance reform - Ahluwalia.
newsitem.headline: India hopes for more insurance reform - Ahluwalia.

text.p: Indian Finance Secretary Montek Singh Ahluwalia said on Friday that he was hopeful of further reforms to open up the insurance sector despite political opposition.

Ahluwalia, answering a question at a business conference on slow progress in opening up insurance and other financial services, said the government also hoped to allow the entry of private pension funds.

"In all these issues we are dealing with a system in which there is a high degree of political participation," Ahluwalia said, referring to criticism by opposition parties of the government's efforts to open up financial services.
"I am quite hopeful that we will see the opening up of all these sectors...and pension funds," he said.
Ahluwalia is the highest ranking civil servant in the Finance Ministry.
The government faces opposition from leftwing parties and trade unions to its efforts to allow private firms in the insurance sector.
In his budget for 1997/98 (April-March) presented on February 28, Finance Minister P. Chidambaram proposed allowing private Indian firms to enter the health insurance sector.
But he did not indicate whether foreign firms would be allowed into health insurance.
Chidambaram also announced that state-controlled Unit Trust of India would be allowed to convert a retirement plan into a full-fledged pension fund.
